headline: Transcriptomic tools benchmarked against established references and orthogonal data
label: Transcriptomic Methods And Benchmarking
summary: Recent work pairs new normalization, differential expression and quantification tools with explicit validation against established references.
synthesis: The common thread is computational methodology for transcriptome quantification and interpretation, with most items pairing a tool with explicit benchmarking against an established reference. gecco proposes gene-specific exponent-corrected library-size normalization for bulk RNA-seq, and pylimma ports limma to AnnData, validated against R across 227 function comparisons. MKMC performs reference-free k-mer analysis that matches alignment-based differential expression and age prediction. TEscape pairs MAS-ISO-seq long-read sequencing across six human cell types with transposable element annotation, while targeted tumor RNA-seq workflows are benchmarked against total RNA-seq. What is new is calibration of expression estimates against orthogonal measurements and reference-free representations: one atlas matches scRNA-seq to Human Protein Atlas immunohistochemistry, and the Blood RNA Stability Atlas classifies 6,064 blood RNAs into stable trait and dynamic state categories.
